S6FL00640.name: Ashley Moody
S6FL00640.bio: U.S. Senator from Florida and former Florida Attorney General.

positions.stance: Says she has spent her career "putting criminals behind bars, standing with our brave law enforcement officers" and making Florida safer.
"I'm fighting for Florida families to keep more of what they earn"; cites no tax on tips and Social Security.
Pledges to keep Florida "the freest state in the nation – a place built on economic freedom and safety in our communities."
"I'll keep fighting to cut the red tape and outdated regulations standing between our growers and their success."

source.label: press releases on their campaign site

S6OH00304.name: Jon Husted
S6OH00304.bio: Former Ohio lieutenant governor, secretary of state, and speaker of the Ohio House.

positions.stance: "I'll always stand with our police, secure the border and fight for the safety of Ohio families."
Says he will keep "standing up for responsible gun owners" and push back on Washington efforts that chip away at Second Amendment freedoms.
"Our small businesses are the backbone of Ohio's economy and they can always count on me to fight for them."
"I've fought to protect family farms and keep agriculture strong," and will keep standing up for farmers and ranchers.

source.label: press releases on their campaign site

positions.stance: Calls for "banning secret and corporate money from our politics."
Calls for "restoring American leadership toward peace and human rights in the world."
Calls for "guaranteeing health care for every single American."
Pledges "a defense of voting rights so fierce that no plot against the franchise can foil the will of the people."
"We need to restore checks and balances in Washington. We need to address this cost of living crisis."

source.label: press releases on their campaign site

S6GA00390.name: Mike Collins
S6GA00390.bio: U.S. Representative from Georgia who built a Jackson-based trucking company with his wife.

positions.stance: Plans to "get rid of the policies that have fueled high prices," including his PERMIT Act to cut red tape for infrastructure and housing.
Would "expand President Trump's energy policies" with "an all the above approach to energy" to lower costs.
Would lower childcare and health care costs through price transparency, lower prescription drug prices, expanded health savings accounts, and cutting waste and fraud.
Supports an agenda "where we protect our borders and fight crime."

source.label: press releases on their campaign site

positions.stance: Will stay "laser-focused on the economy, jobs, and making life more affordable."
"We will clean up Washington and hold politicians in both parties accountable."
"I'll push term limits."
Would "make Congress pay for the full cost of their healthcare."
Would "cut Congress' pay if they vote to shut down the government."

source.label: press releases on their campaign site

S6ME00159.name: Susan Collins
S6ME00159.bio: Five-term U.S. Senator from Maine and chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee.

positions.stance: "I am working to lower prescription drug costs for our seniors."
Working "to build more housing so your kids can build their lives here."
"I have always worked across the aisle."
"I don't work for any president. I work for you."
"I believe America is crying out for compromise and less chaos."

source.label: an op-ed they wrote, reposted on their campaign site

S4AK00214.name: Dan S. Sullivan
S4AK00214.bio: U.S. Senator from Alaska serving on the Armed Services, Commerce, Veterans Affairs, and Environment and Public Works committees.

positions.stance: "I'm fighting to stop members of Congress from cashing in as DC lobbyists."
Calls for "a temporary pause of American diesel exports" to rebuild reserves ahead of winter.
"The best way to bring down energy prices for Alaskans is to produce more energy in Alaska, by Alaskans, for Alaskans."
Says he has fought to cut taxes, reduce burdensome regulations and unleash Alaskan energy, and "will keep fighting" for Alaska's businesses and workers.

source.label: press releases on their campaign site

S6AK00326.name: Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.
S6AK00326.bio: Former U.S. Forest Service worker and elementary school teacher from Petersburg, Alaska.

positions.stance: Says political division "needs to be addressed with pragmatic, bipartisan cooperation to move our country forward."
Proposes easing rules on manufactured homes, rural utility infrastructure aid, low-interest loans for first-time buyers, and more vocational education for tradespeople.
Says haphazard tariffs and "an ill conceived war in Iran" have spiked energy and commodity prices.
Supports "bipartisan immigration reform" with legal pathways to citizenship, strong border protection using technology, and refusing entry to or deporting violent criminals.
"I would support efforts to overturn Citizen United."

source.label: their League of Women Voters questionnaire, posted on their campaign site

S6WY00209.name: Harriet Hageman
S6WY00209.bio: U.S. Representative for Wyoming and member of the House Judiciary and Natural Resources Committees.

positions.stance: Opposes Washington policies she says burden ranchers, including Endangered Species Act abuse, the WOTUS rule, and mandated electronic livestock tracking.
"Border security is national security"; calls ending the "invasion of our country" among her top priorities.
"We are not taxed too little; we spend too much"; rejects budgets with unchecked deficit spending and seeks House budget reforms.
Supports coal, oil, gas and uranium, and reforming the National Environmental Policy Act to "unleash American energy."
Says education should focus on reading, writing and arithmetic; advocates for "the sanctity of human life from conception to natural death."
